turns.doctor_question: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
turns.patient_response:
Nice to meet you, doctor. Well, I came in because... honestly, I feel like I’m falling apart lately. 

They recently changed my hours at the warehouse where I work, and they put in this new inventory system. Ever since then, things have just gone downhill. I'm missing shifts, which isn't like me, and I'm skipping out on my church commitments, too. I keep snapping at my family for no good reason. Some mornings, I just sit there on the edge of the bed in my work boots, just... wondering if I can even face going into that place anymore.

symptom_reasoning.S081: The patient describes emotional and behavioral difficulties, including missing work shifts and commitments, in direct response to identifiable workplace stressors (changed hours and a new inventory system).
symptom_reasoning.S060: The patient reports repeatedly snapping at their family for no good reason, indicating snappiness and heightened irritability.

turns.doctor_question: Do you feel these problems started because of the changes at work?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, I do. I really started coming apart within the first few weeks after they changed my hours and brought in that new inventory system. Before that, I was doing just fine. I was keeping my routine together and handling all my responsibilities without any trouble. But once they made those changes... that's when everything just derailed.

symptom_reasoning.S081: The patient confirms that their difficulties began directly in response to an identifiable psychosocial stressor (work schedule and system changes) within weeks of its occurrence.

turns.doctor_question: Lately, have you been feeling down or depressed?
turns.patient_response: No, I wouldn't really say I feel depressed. I don't feel sad or down, if that's what you mean. It's more... I'm just incredibly stressed out and frustrated that I can't seem to get a handle on things right now.

symptom_reasoning.S024: The patient explicitly states that they do not feel depressed, sad, or down.

turns.doctor_question: Do you feel anxious or on edge a lot of the time lately?
turns.patient_response: Not really, no. I wouldn't say I feel anxious or nervous. I don't get... jumpy or anything like that. Like I said, it's really just that overwhelming frustration about the whole situation at the warehouse. I just can't seem to make it all work anymore, but I wouldn't call it being on edge.

symptom_reasoning.S056: The patient explicitly denies experiencing anxiety or feeling nervous.
symptom_reasoning.S058: The patient explicitly states they do not feel jumpy or on edge.

turns.doctor_question: Since the changes at work, have you done things that break rules or go against what’s expected of you, other than missing shifts?
turns.patient_response: No, no. I haven't done anything like that. I mean, besides not showing up for those shifts, I'm not breaking any rules or... acting out, or whatever. I've always been one to do what's expected of me. It's just that right now, with the way they changed everything, I just can't seem to manage it. But I'm not causing trouble on purpose.
